title: Cristiano Ronaldo says he is ‘very happy’ at Al Nassr: ‘I belong to Saudi Arabia’
content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has said he is “very happy” in Saudi Arabia and wants to stay after a disagreement earlier this month over how Al Nassr is managed.

Ronaldo, 41, missed league wins against Al Riyadh and Al Ittihad as he felt let down by the club’s hierarchy following a perceived failure to strengthen the squad during the January transfer window.

The Portugal international returned to the field as captain against Al Fateh, ending a three-game absence by scoring in the 2-0 win. Following Saturday’s win against Al Hazem, which sent Al Nassr to the top of the league, he spoke about his future in Saudi Arabia.

“I’m very happy,” Ronaldo told Saudi broadcaster Thmanyah after the match. “As I say so many times, I belong to Saudi Arabia.

“It’s a country that has welcomed me very well, and my family and my friends. I’m happy here, I want to continue here.

“The most important thing is we keep pushing (for the league title), we are there at the top. We do our job, we win, make pressure, let’s see at the end of the season.”

Ronaldo has been in the Saudi Pro League since December 2022 when he joined from Manchester United, and he had a €50million release clause inserted in the new two-year contract he signed in June.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner had felt let down by the lack of ambition shown by Al Nassr, who are one of four clubs majority-owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside Al Ittihad, Al Ahli and Al Hilal.

The club signed Saudi Arabia international Abdullah Al-Hamdan from Al Hilal and Iraqi midfielder Haydeer Abdulkareem from Al-Zawraa SC over the winter window. Meanwhile, Ronaldo’s former Real Madrid team-mate Karim Benzema left Al Ittihad to join Al Hilal.

During the forward’s absence from the squad, the Saudi Pro League released a statement saying “no individual – however significant – determines decisions beyond their own club”.

Al Nassr are top of the league having won their past eight matches, one point above Al Hilal after 22 games. They are also through to the quarter finals of the AFC Asian Cup where they will face UAE Pro League side Al Wasl.
